newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House budget chief says must see accord soon.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House budget chief says must see accord soon.

text.p: House Budget Committee chairman John Kasich said Wednesday a budget agreement must be reached with the White House by the middle of next week or Republicans will offer their own balanced budget plan.
Kasich said his talks with administration officials have been very positive. "We have been able to establish a level of trust," he said in a speech before the Independent Insurance Agents.
The Ohio Republican said he believed it would be possible to reach an accord to balance the budget in five years, but he said the administration would need to offer more changes.
"We will know into the middle of next week whether we can reach an agreement," Kasich said.

He also reiterated his view that tax rates should be reduced as part of a tax cut included in the budget. "The marginal rates are too high. The incentive to go to work has been reduced," he said. Kasich went further to state that tax rates were too high in part because of increased benefits provided to senior citizens over the last 30-40 years. "We need to achieve some generational balance," he said.
